/-!
# The base-field window transport pack — DDR-2's `N`-pack (DAT-D `dd4`/`ddr`)

The abstract fibre window divisor `N` of DDR-2's certified-degree pinch
(`RiemannRoch/CarveDegree.lean`), built for any field extension `K/k`: an honest Weil
divisor on `relCurve C K` carrying the **transported** DD-0 window facts of the `k`-level
embedding window `M·F`.  Per I-0204's binding architectural finding, the per-field ledger
constants do *not* transport (`windowM_choice` is a per-field `Classical.choose`), so `N`
is produced by transporting window **facts**, not by re-running the `K`-level ledger:

* the `k`-level `H¹` inputs enter through the landed twist-pair collapse
  (`relThetaPairH1_windowM`, `subsingleton_relThetaPairH1`) and cross into the datum
  world by the whole-chart theta datum (`Cohomology/RelCurveCollapse.lean`);
* the datum base-changes to `K` (`datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange`), where the
  presentation bridge (`presentationSheafIso` + `subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_one_iff`)
  extracts an honest divisor `windowTransportDivisor C K π a` with vanishing `H¹`;
* its class is the transported theta class (`cechPicClass_baseChange` + the collapse
  class law), so its degree is `a·δ` by E-iv-alg
  (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) and W7-B3 (`classDeg_cechPicMap_of_isIso`);
* the `K`-level normalization windows come from the π-free peeling
  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness`, the abstract-witness form of DAT-0a's
  `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) at the transported
  multiplier window `s·F`, licensed by ledger arithmetic.

## The `N`-pack (DDR-2's threaded hypotheses, exact spellings)

At `N := windowN C K π hπ g = windowTransportDivisor C K π (windowM_choice π hπ g)`:

* `hNwin` — `subsingleton_h1_windowN` : `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(N))`;
* `hNdeg` — `two_mul_genus_le_deg_windowN` : `2g ≤ deg K N`;
* `hNnorm` — `subsingleton_h1_windowN_sub` : `∀ D', deg D' ≤ 2g → Subsingleton
  H¹(𝒪(N − D'))`;
* `hNrank` — `h0_windowN` : `h⁰_K(𝒪(N)) = h⁰_k(𝒪(M·F))`.

The remaining threaded hypothesis of `deg_divFamDivisor_of_carve` supplied elsewhere is
`hdict` (the sections dictionary at the field point, DD-4 Task 5 field content — still
open), besides the sibling seams `hsurj`/`hpair`.
-/

9	/-!
10	# Adelic Riemann–Roch lane — the χ-ledger (nodes N13, N14)
11	
12	This file implements the Tier-2 χ-ledger nodes of the adelic Riemann–Roch lane
13	(design document §3, nodes N13–N16), built on top of the Tier-0 substrate
14	`AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Adelic.Substrate` (`sectionOfDivisor`,
15	`linearSystem`, `pointValuation`, the `order` laws).
16	
17	Everything here lives inside the fixed function field `K = K(X)` as
18	`AddSubgroup K(X)` — the "function-field model" of the design.  For a chosen
19	two-open cover `U₀, U₁` of `X` with overlap `V := U₀ ⊓ U₁` and a Weil divisor
20	`D`, the four cover-adelic objects are
21	
22	* `Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) = sectionOfDivisor U₀ D`, `Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D)) = sectionOfDivisor U₁ D`;
23	* the **cover adele** `𝒜(D) := Γ(V, 𝒪(D)) = sectionOfDivisor V D`;
24	* the **coboundary** `B(D) := Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D)) = coboundary U₀ U₁ D`,
25	  which lies inside `𝒜(D)` (`coboundary_le_overlap`);
26	* the **linear system** `L(D) := Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D)) = linearSystem D`
27	  (kernel of the Čech difference map, `= Γ(⊤, 𝒪(D))` when `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`), which
28	  also lies inside `𝒜(D)` (`linearSystem_le_overlap`);
29	* the **cover cohomology** `Ȟ¹(D) := 𝒜(D) ⧸ B(D) = H1 U₀ U₁ D`.
30	
31	## N13 — the twist ledger
32	
33	For `D ≤ D'` with the added part `D' − D` supported on the overlap `V`, the
34	inclusions of section subgroups assemble into the four-term exact sequence
35	
36	```
37	0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0.
38	```
39	
40	The **exactness at the `L`-terms** — the injectivity of the window map
41	`L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D)` — is the concrete kernel computation
42	`L(D') ⊓ 𝒜(D) = L(D)` (`linearSystem_inf_overlap_eq`): a global section of
43	`𝒪(D')` that is already `D`-bounded on the overlap is a global section of
44	`𝒪(D)`, because off the overlap `D = D'`.  This is pure `AddSubgroup`
45	lattice algebra over `K`, the design's "elementary Submodule" assessment.  The
46	window map, the coboundary functoriality `Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')` and the connecting
47	homomorphism are set up concretely (`windowMap`, `H1Twist`, `windowConnect`);
48	the surjectivity at `Ȟ¹(D')` is the Mittag-Leffler/affine-cover input
49	`𝒜(D') = 𝒜(D) + B(D')`, deferred to the finiteness wave.
50	
51	## N14 — the local step is bounded by the residue degree
52	
53	For a single prime divisor `P` and the one-step twist `D + P`, the local quotient
54	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D + P)) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` injects into the single-point valuation quotient
55	`G(P, −n−1) ⧸ G(P, −n)` (`localStepQuot_injective`), which the DVR structure at
56	`P` identifies with the residue field `κ(P)`; hence its `k`-dimension is at most
57	`deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.
58	
59	## References
60	
61	Design document `adelic-rr-lane-design.md` §§2–3, nodes N13–N16; Stichtenoth,
62	*Algebraic Function Fields and Codes*, ch. 1; Serre, *Groupes algébriques et
63	corps de classes*, ch. II (répartitions); Hartshorne, *Algebraic Geometry* II §6.
64	-/

83	/-- **Antitonicity in the open.** Enlarging the open imposes *more* order
84	conditions, so `Γ(U', 𝒪(D)) ⊆ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` whenever `U ≤ U'`.  (The section
85	subgroup is antitone in the open and monotone in the divisor.) -/
86	theorem sectionOfDivisor_antitone_open {U U' : X.Opens} (h : U ≤ U')
87	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) : sectionOfDivisor U' D ≤ sectionOfDivisor U D := by
88	  intro f hf
89	  rcases hf with rfl | hf
90	  · exact Or.inl rfl
91	  · exact Or.inr fun P hP => hf P (h hP)
92	
93	variable (U₀ U₁ : X.Opens)
94	
95	/-- **The coboundary subgroup `B(D) = Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) + Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D))`.** The image of
96	the Čech difference-of-restrictions map for the cover `{U₀, U₁}`, realised inside
97	`K` as the sum of the two chart section subgroups. -/
98	noncomputable def coboundary (D : X.WeilDivisor) : AddSubgroup X.functionField :=
99	  sectionOfDivisor U₀ D ⊔ sectionOfDivisor U₁ D
100	
101	/-- **The coboundary lands in the overlap sections.** `B(D) ⊆ 𝒜(D) = Γ(V, 𝒪(D))`:
102	each chart section restricts to the overlap. -/
103	theorem coboundary_le_overlap (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
104	    coboundary U₀ U₁ D ≤ sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D :=
105	  sup_le (sectionOfDivisor_antitone_open inf_le_left D)
106	    (sectionOfDivisor_antitone_open inf_le_right D)
107	
108	/-- **The linear system lands in the overlap sections.** `L(D) ⊆ 𝒜(D)`: a global
109	section restricts to the overlap. -/
110	theorem linearSystem_le_overlap (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
111	    linearSystem D ≤ sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D :=
112	  sectionOfDivisor_antitone_open le_top D
113	
114	/-- **N13 — exactness at the `L`-terms (window-map injectivity).**  Suppose
115	`D ≤ D'` pointwise and the added part `D' − D` is supported on the overlap
116	`V = U₀ ⊓ U₁` (`hsupp`: off `V`, `D` and `D'` agree).  Then a global section of
117	`𝒪(D')` that is already `D`-bounded on the overlap `V` is a global section of
118	`𝒪(D)`:
119	`L(D') ⊓ 𝒜(D) = L(D)`.
120	
121	This is the concrete kernel computation showing the window map
122	`L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D)` is injective (exactness of the ledger sequence at the
123	two left `L`-terms).  Pure `AddSubgroup` lattice algebra over `K`: on the overlap
124	the `D`-bound comes from membership in `𝒜(D)`; off the overlap `D(P) = D'(P)`, so
125	the global `D'`-bound *is* the `D`-bound. -/
126	theorem linearSystem_inf_overlap_eq {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
127	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
128	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)
129	    (hsupp : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) →
130	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
131	    linearSystem D' ⊓ sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D = linearSystem D := by
132	  apply le_antisymm
133	  · intro f hf
134	    obtain ⟨hf1, hf2⟩ := AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mp hf
135	    have hf1' : f ∈ sectionOfDivisor (⊤ : X.Opens) D' := hf1
136	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
137	    · exact (linearSystem D).zero_mem
138	    change f ∈ sectionOfDivisor (⊤ : X.Opens) D
139	    rw [mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne]
140	    intro P _
141	    by_cases hPV : P.point ∈ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens)
142	    · exact (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf2 P hPV
143	    · rw [hsupp P hPV]
144	      exact (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf1' P
145	        (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_top P.point)
146	  · exact le_inf (sectionOfDivisor_mono ⊤ hle) (linearSystem_le_overlap U₀ U₁ D)
147	
148	/-- **Monotonicity of the coboundary in the divisor.** `D ≤ D' ⇒ B(D) ⊆ B(D')`. -/
149	theorem coboundary_mono {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
150	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
151	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
152	    coboundary U₀ U₁ D ≤ coboundary U₀ U₁ D' :=
153	  sup_le_sup (sectionOfDivisor_mono U₀ hle) (sectionOfDivisor_mono U₁ hle)
154	
155	/-! ### The cover cohomology `Ȟ¹(D)` and its twist maps -/
156	
157	/-- **The cover cohomology `Ȟ¹(D) = 𝒜(D) / B(D)`.** The cokernel of the Čech
158	difference map, realised as the quotient of the overlap sections `𝒜(D)` by the
159	coboundary `B(D)` (which is a subgroup of `𝒜(D)` by `coboundary_le_overlap`).
160	This is the function-field-model incarnation of `AffineCoverMVSquare.H1Cok`. -/
161	def H1 (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Type u :=
162	  (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D) ⧸
163	    (coboundary U₀ U₁ D).addSubgroupOf (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)
164	
165	noncomputable instance instAddCommGroupH1 (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
166	    AddCommGroup (H1 U₀ U₁ D) :=
167	  inferInstanceAs (AddCommGroup (_ ⧸
168	    (coboundary U₀ U₁ D).addSubgroupOf (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D)))
169	
170	/-- **Functoriality of `Ȟ¹` in the divisor (the H¹-inclusion map).** For `D ≤ D'`
171	the inclusions `𝒜(D) ⊆ 𝒜(D')`, `B(D) ⊆ B(D')` induce the comparison map
172	`Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D')`.  This is the right-hand map of the ledger sequence
173	`… → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0` (the AG mirror of the DG `H1TailIncl`). -/
174	noncomputable def H1Twist {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
175	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
176	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
177	    H1 U₀ U₁ D →+ H1 U₀ U₁ D' :=
178	  QuotientAddGroup.map _ _
179	    (AddSubgroup.inclusion (sectionOfDivisor_mono (U₀ ⊓ U₁) hle)) (by
180	      intro g hg
181	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf] at hg
182	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_comap, AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf, AddSubgroup.coe_inclusion]
183	      exact coboundary_mono U₀ U₁ hle hg)
184	
185	/-- **The window map `L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D)`.** Induced by the inclusion of
186	global sections into the overlap sections `L(D') ⊆ 𝒜(D')` (`linearSystem_le_overlap`),
187	compatibly with `L(D) ⊆ 𝒜(D)`.  This is the left-hand map of the ledger sequence
188	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → …` (the AG mirror of the DG `windowMap`). -/
189	noncomputable def windowMap {D D' : X.WeilDivisor} :
190	    (linearSystem D' ⧸
191	        (linearSystem D).addSubgroupOf (linearSystem D')) →+
192	      (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D' ⧸
193	        (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D).addSubgroupOf (sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D')) :=
194	  QuotientAddGroup.map _ _
195	    (AddSubgroup.inclusion (linearSystem_le_overlap U₀ U₁ D')) (by
196	      intro g hg
197	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf] at hg
198	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_comap, AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf, AddSubgroup.coe_inclusion]
199	      exact linearSystem_le_overlap U₀ U₁ D hg)
200	
201	/-- **N13 — exactness at the `L`-terms, packaged as window-map injectivity.**
202	Under `D ≤ D'` with `D' − D` supported on the overlap, the window map
203	`L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D)` is injective.  This is `linearSystem_inf_overlap_eq`
204	transported into the quotient language: the ledger sequence is exact at both
205	`L`-terms. -/
206	theorem windowMap_injective {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
207	    (hle : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
208	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)
209	    (hsupp : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∉ (U₀ ⊓ U₁ : X.Opens) →
210	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
211	    Function.Injective (windowMap (D := D) (D' := D') U₀ U₁) := by
212	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
213	  intro q
214	  induction q using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on with
215	  | H g =>
216	    intro hq
217	    simp only [windowMap, QuotientAddGroup.map_mk, QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff,
218	      AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf, AddSubgroup.coe_inclusion] at hq
219	    rw [QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff, AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf]
220	    have hmem : (g : X.functionField) ∈ linearSystem D' ⊓ sectionOfDivisor (U₀ ⊓ U₁) D :=
221	      AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mpr ⟨g.2, hq⟩
222	    rwa [linearSystem_inf_overlap_eq U₀ U₁ hle hsupp] at hmem
223	
224	end Ledger

226	/-! ## §N14. The local step is bounded by the residue degree
227	
228	For a single prime divisor `P` and the one-step twist raising the pole bound at
229	`P` by one, the local quotient `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` injects into the
230	single-point valuation quotient `orderGe P (-n-1) ⧸ orderGe P (-n)`.  The DVR
231	structure at `P` identifies the latter with the residue field `κ(P)` (one
232	uniformizer step ⇒ one copy of `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P`), whose `k`-dimension is
233	`deg P = [κ(P) : k]`; hence `dim_k (Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))) ≤ deg P`.  This
234	file supplies the **elementary (residue-field-free) core**: the single-point
235	subgroups, the local identity `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⊓ orderGe P (-n)`, and
236	the resulting injection.  The residue-field identification of the target and the
237	numerical `[κ(P):k]` count is the DVR step layered on top. -/
238	
239	section LocalStep
240	
241	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
242	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
243	
244	/-- **The single-point order-≥-`m` subgroup.** `orderGe P m = { f ∈ K : ord_P f ≥ m }`
245	(with the zero function admitted separately, the `ord_P 0 = +∞` convention).  For
246	`m ≤ 0` this is the fractional ideal `𝔪_P^{-m}` of the DVR `𝒪_P` viewed inside
247	`K`; the consecutive quotient `orderGe P m / orderGe P (m+1)` is one copy of the
248	residue field `κ(P)`.  Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric. -/
249	def orderGe (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) : AddSubgroup X.functionField where
250	  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ m ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }
251	  zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
252	  add_mem' := by
253	    intro a b ha hb
254	    rcases eq_or_ne a 0 with rfl | hane
255	    · simpa using hb
256	    rcases eq_or_ne b 0 with rfl | hbne
257	    · simpa using ha
258	    rcases eq_or_ne (a + b) 0 with h0 | h0
259	    · exact Or.inl h0
260	    exact Or.inr ((le_min (ha.resolve_left hane) (hb.resolve_left hbne)).trans
261	      (order_add_ge_min P hane hbne h0))
262	  neg_mem' := by
263	    intro a ha
264	    rcases ha with rfl | ha
265	    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
266	    · exact Or.inr (by rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_neg]; exact ha)
267	
268	theorem mem_orderGe {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ} {f : X.functionField} :
269	    f ∈ orderGe P m ↔ f = 0 ∨ m ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f :=
270	  Iff.rfl
271	
272	theorem mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ} {f : X.functionField}
273	    (hf : f ≠ 0) : f ∈ orderGe P m ↔ m ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f := by
274	  rw [mem_orderGe, or_iff_right hf]
275	
276	/-- **Antitonicity in the lower bound.** A larger order bound is a stronger
277	condition, so `orderGe P m' ⊆ orderGe P m` whenever `m ≤ m'`. -/
278	theorem orderGe_antitone {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m m' : ℤ} (h : m ≤ m') :
279	    orderGe P m' ≤ orderGe P m := by
280	  intro f hf
281	  rcases hf with rfl | hf
282	  · exact Or.inl rfl
283	  · exact Or.inr (h.trans hf)
284	
285	/-- **N14 — the local step identity.** Let `D ≤ D'` be two divisors differing
286	only at the prime divisor `P` (`hoff`), where `D'` has exactly one more pole
287	(`hstep : D'(P) = D(P) + 1`), and let `P ∈ U`.  Then a section of `𝒪(D')` on `U`
288	lies in `𝒪(D)` exactly when it also satisfies the tighter bound `ord_P f ≥ -D(P)`:
289	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⊓ orderGe P (-D(P))`.
290	
291	This is the kernel computation exhibiting the local step quotient
292	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) / Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` as a subquotient at the single point `P`. -/
293	theorem sectionOfDivisor_inf_orderGe {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
294	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
295	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
296	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
297	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
298	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q) :
299	    sectionOfDivisor U D =
300	      sectionOfDivisor U D' ⊓ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) := by
301	  apply le_antisymm
302	  · intro f hf
303	    refine AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mpr ⟨sectionOfDivisor_mono U hle hf, ?_⟩
304	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
305	    · exact Or.inl rfl
306	    exact Or.inr ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf P hPU)
307	  · intro f hf
308	    obtain ⟨hf1, hf2⟩ := AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mp hf
309	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
310	    · exact (sectionOfDivisor U D).zero_mem
311	    rw [mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne]
312	    intro Q hQU
313	    by_cases hQP : Q = P
314	    · subst hQP
315	      exact (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf2
316	    · rw [hoff Q hQP]
317	      exact (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf1 Q hQU
318	
319	/-- **N14 — the section lands in the one-step-looser single-point subgroup.** A
320	section of `𝒪(D')` on `U` (with `P ∈ U` and `D'(P) = D(P) + 1`) has order at least
321	`-D(P) - 1` at `P`, i.e. lies in `orderGe P (-D(P) - 1)`. -/
322	theorem sectionOfDivisor_le_orderGe {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
323	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
324	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
325	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1) :
326	    sectionOfDivisor U D' ≤ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) := by
327	  intro f hf
328	  rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
329	  · exact Or.inl rfl
330	  refine Or.inr ?_
331	  have := (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hfne).mp hf P hPU
332	  rw [hstep] at this
333	  linarith
334	
335	/-- **N14 — the local step quotient injects into the single-point valuation
336	quotient.**  Under the one-step hypotheses of `sectionOfDivisor_inf_orderGe`, the
337	inclusion of section subgroups induces a map
338	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) / Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) → orderGe P (-D(P)-1) / orderGe P (-D(P))`, and it is
339	injective.  This is the **exact local structure** of node N14: the local step
340	quotient is a subgroup of the single-point valuation quotient
341	`𝔪_P^{-n-1}/𝔪_P^{-n} ≅ κ(P)`, whence `dim_k` of the step is at most
342	`deg P = [κ(P):k]` (the residue-field identification of the target and the
343	numerical bound is the DVR layer on top of this reduction). -/
344	noncomputable def localStepQuot {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
345	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
346	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
347	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1) :
348	    (sectionOfDivisor U D' ⧸
349	        (sectionOfDivisor U D).addSubgroupOf (sectionOfDivisor U D')) →+
350	      (orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) ⧸
351	        (orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)).addSubgroupOf
352	          (orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1))) :=
353	  QuotientAddGroup.map _ _
354	    (AddSubgroup.inclusion (sectionOfDivisor_le_orderGe hPU hstep)) (by
355	      intro g hg
356	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf] at hg
357	      rw [AddSubgroup.mem_comap, AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf, AddSubgroup.coe_inclusion]
358	      rcases eq_or_ne (g : X.functionField) 0 with h0 | h0
359	      · rw [h0]; exact (orderGe _ _).zero_mem
360	      exact (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero h0).mpr
361	        ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero h0).mp hg P hPU))
362	
363	theorem localStepQuot_injective {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
364	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
365	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
366	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
367	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
368	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
369	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
370	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q) :
371	    Function.Injective (localStepQuot hPU hstep) := by
372	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
373	  intro q
374	  induction q using QuotientAddGroup.induction_on with
375	  | H g =>
376	    intro hq
377	    simp only [localStepQuot, QuotientAddGroup.map_mk, QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff,
378	      AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf, AddSubgroup.coe_inclusion] at hq
379	    rw [QuotientAddGroup.eq_zero_iff, AddSubgroup.mem_addSubgroupOf]
380	    have hmem : (g : X.functionField) ∈
381	        sectionOfDivisor U D' ⊓ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) :=
382	      AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mpr ⟨g.2, hq⟩
383	    rwa [← sectionOfDivisor_inf_orderGe hPU hle hoff] at hmem
384	
385	end LocalStep
386	
387	/-! ## §N14b. The residue-degree bound on the local step
388	
389	The `LocalStep` section reduced the local step quotient to the single-point
390	valuation quotient `orderGe P m ⧸ orderGe P (m+1)` (with `m = -n-1`).  We now
391	identify this target with the residue field `κ(P)` of the DVR stalk `𝒪_P` and
392	read off the numerical bound `dim_k ≤ deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.
393	
394	The DVR bridges below connect the additive order `ord_P = -log ∘ v_P` to
395	integrality in the stalk `𝒪_P = 𝒪_{X,P}`: a nonzero rational function has
396	nonnegative order at `P` exactly when it is a section of the stalk. -/
397	
398	section LocalDegree
399	
400	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
401	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
402	
403	/-- **Order-nonnegativity is stalk-integrality.** For a nonzero rational function
404	`f`, `ord_P f ≥ 0` exactly when `f` lifts to the DVR stalk `𝒪_P = 𝒪_{X,P}`, i.e.
405	`f = a` for some `a ∈ 𝒪_P` (viewed in `K` via the fraction-field embedding). This
406	is the additive-normalisation reading of `v_P(f) ≤ 1 ⟺ f ∈ 𝒪_P`. -/
407	theorem exists_stalk_lift_of_order_nonneg {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
408	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0)
409	    (hord : 0 ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) :
410	    ∃ a : X.presheaf.stalk P.point,
411	      algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk P.point) X.functionField a = f := by
412	  have hpv : pointValuation P f ≠ 0 := by
413	    simpa using (Valuation.zero_iff (pointValuation P)).not.mpr hf
414	  have hlog : WithZero.log (pointValuation P f) ≤ 0 := by
415	    have := order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation P f
416	    rw [this] at hord; linarith
417	  have hle1 : pointValuation P f ≤ 1 := by
418	    have : WithZero.log (pointValuation P f) ≤ WithZero.log (1 : ℤᵐ⁰) := by
419	      simpa using hlog
420	    exact (WithZero.log_le_log hpv one_ne_zero).mp this
421	  exact IsDiscreteValuationRing.exists_lift_of_le_one hle1
422	
423	/-- **Order surjectivity: every integer is realised as an order at `P`.**  The DVR
424	stalk `𝒪_P` has a uniformizer `π` with `ord_P π = 1` — the maximal-ideal
425	height-one place, whose adic valuation is `exp (-1)` (mathlib's
426	`IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_exists_uniformizer`) — and its integer
427	powers `π^j` realise every order `j : ℤ`.  This is the surjectivity of
428	`ord_P : K(X) → ℤ`; only the intrinsic order value of the DVR uniformizer is used,
429	never a distinguished *global* uniformizer (a fixed rational function). -/
430	theorem exists_order_eq (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (j : ℤ) :
431	    ∃ t : X.functionField, t ≠ 0 ∧ Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = j := by
432	  obtain ⟨π, hπ⟩ :=
433	    (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal
434	      (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)).valuation_exists_uniformizer X.functionField
435	  have hval : pointValuation P π = WithZero.exp (-1 : ℤ) := hπ
436	  have hπ0 : π ≠ 0 := by
437	    rintro rfl
438	    rw [map_zero] at hval
439	    exact WithZero.exp_ne_zero hval.symm
440	  refine ⟨π ^ j, zpow_ne_zero j hπ0, ?_⟩
441	  rw [order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation, map_zpow₀, hval, WithZero.log_zpow,
442	    WithZero.log_exp, smul_eq_mul]
443	  ring
444	
445	end LocalDegree
446	
447	/-! ## §N14c/N15/N16. The `k`-linear χ-ledger over a field of constants
448	
449	The dimension count of the χ-ledger lives over a base field `k` of constants:
450	`k ↪ K(X)` with every nonzero constant a unit at every prime (order `0`
451	everywhere).  Under this hypothesis the section subgroups and single-point
452	subgroups are `k`-subspaces, their subquotients are finite-dimensional `k`-vector
453	spaces (gated by the keystone/finiteness inputs as `[Module.Finite k …]`
454	binders), and the twist ledger telescopes numerically.
455	
456	`k` is the **field of constants** of the curve — algebraically the elements of
457	`K(X)` integral over the ground field and regular at every point; on a smooth
458	proper curve over an algebraically closed `k̄` this is `k̄` itself.  We package the
459	"constants are everywhere-unit" property as the gate `IsConstantField`. -/
460	
461	section BaseField
462	
463	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X]
464	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
465	    [Algebra k X.functionField]
466	
467	/-- **Field-of-constants gate.** Every nonzero constant `c ∈ k ⊆ K(X)` is a unit
468	at every prime divisor `P`, i.e. `ord_P c = 0`.  This is the property that makes
469	`k` a field of constants: constants have neither zeros nor poles.  On a smooth
470	proper curve over `k̄`, with `k = k̄`, it holds because a nonzero constant is a
471	unit in every local ring.  No global instance — an honest gate supplied at use
472	sites (design §4, mirroring `HasDedekindChart`). -/
473	class IsConstantField (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X]
474	    [IsLocallyNoetherian X] [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
475	    [Algebra k X.functionField] : Prop where
476	  /-- Nonzero constants have order zero at every prime divisor. -/
477	  order_algebraMap_eq_zero : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (c : k), c ≠ 0 →
478	    Scheme.RationalMap.order P (algebraMap k X.functionField c) = 0
479	
480	variable [IsConstantField k X]
481	
482	/-- **The section subspace `Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` as a `k`-vector space.** With `k` a field
483	of constants, the additive section subgroup `sectionOfDivisor U D` is closed under
484	multiplication by constants, hence a `k`-submodule of `K(X)`. -/
485	def sectionSub (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) : Submodule k X.functionField where
486	  carrier := sectionOfDivisor U D
487	  add_mem' := (sectionOfDivisor U D).add_mem
488	  zero_mem' := (sectionOfDivisor U D).zero_mem
489	  smul_mem' c f hf := by
490	    rw [Algebra.smul_def]
491	    rcases eq_or_ne c 0 with rfl | hc
492	    · simp
493	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
494	    · simp
495	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
496	    rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P
497	        (by simpa using (map_ne_zero (algebraMap k X.functionField)).mpr hc) hf0,
498	      IsConstantField.order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc, zero_add]
499	    exact (mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf P hP
500	
501	/-- **The single-point subspace `orderGe P m` as a `k`-vector space.** -/
502	def orderGeSub (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) : Submodule k X.functionField where
503	  carrier := orderGe P m
504	  add_mem' := (orderGe P m).add_mem
505	  zero_mem' := (orderGe P m).zero_mem
506	  smul_mem' c f hf := by
507	    rw [Algebra.smul_def]
508	    rcases eq_or_ne c 0 with rfl | hc
509	    · simp
510	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hf0
511	    · simp
512	    refine Or.inr ?_
513	    rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P
514	        (by simpa using (map_ne_zero (algebraMap k X.functionField)).mpr hc) hf0,
515	      IsConstantField.order_algebraMap_eq_zero P c hc, zero_add]
516	    exact (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hf0).mp hf
517	
518	@[simp] theorem mem_sectionSub {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
519	    {f : X.functionField} : f ∈ sectionSub k U D ↔ f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D := Iff.rfl
520	
521	@[simp] theorem mem_orderGeSub {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ} {f : X.functionField} :
522	    f ∈ orderGeSub k P m ↔ f ∈ orderGe P m := Iff.rfl
523	
524	/-- **Monotonicity of `sectionSub` in the divisor.** -/
525	theorem sectionSub_mono (U : X.Opens) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
526	    (h : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
527	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
528	    sectionSub k U D ≤ sectionSub k U D' :=
529	  fun _ hx => sectionOfDivisor_mono U h hx
530	
531	/-- **The local step `k`-vector space `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))`.** The relative
532	quotient of the two section subspaces; this is `ℓ(D')/ℓ(D)`-space whose dimension
533	the χ-ledger telescopes. -/
534	abbrev localStepDom (U : X.Opens) (D D' : X.WeilDivisor) : Type u :=
535	  ↥(sectionSub k U D') ⧸ Submodule.comap (sectionSub k U D').subtype (sectionSub k U D)
536	
537	/-- **The single-point valuation subquotient `orderGe P (m-1) ⧸ orderGe P m`.**
538	By the DVR structure at `P` this one-uniformizer-step quotient is a copy of the
539	residue field `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P` (antitone convention: `orderGe P m ⊆ orderGe P (m-1)`). -/
540	abbrev localStepTgt (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) : Type u :=
541	  ↥(orderGeSub k P (m - 1)) ⧸
542	    Submodule.comap (orderGeSub k P (m - 1)).subtype (orderGeSub k P m)
543	
544	/-- **The `k`-linear local step map.** The `k`-linear upgrade of `localStepQuot`:
545	induced by the inclusion `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⊆ orderGe P (-D(P)-1)` on the relative
546	quotients, mapping the local step subquotient
547	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` `k`-linearly into `orderGe P (-D(P)-1) ⧸ orderGe P (-D(P))`. -/
548	noncomputable def localStepMapₖ {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
549	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
550	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
551	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1) :
552	    localStepDom k U D D' →ₗ[k]
553	      localStepTgt k P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) :=
554	  Submodule.mapQ _ _
555	    (Submodule.inclusion (fun x hx => sectionOfDivisor_le_orderGe hPU hstep hx)) (by
556	      intro g hg
557	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, mem_sectionSub] at hg
558	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
559	        Submodule.coe_inclusion, mem_orderGeSub]
560	      rcases eq_or_ne (g : X.functionField) 0 with h0 | h0
561	      · rw [h0]; exact (orderGe _ _).zero_mem
562	      exact (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero h0).mpr
563	        ((mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero h0).mp hg P hPU))
564	
565	/-- **The `k`-linear local step map is injective** (N14 — `k`-linear form). The
566	kernel computation `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) = Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⊓ orderGe P (-D(P))`
567	(`sectionOfDivisor_inf_orderGe`) transported to the relative quotients. -/
568	theorem localStepMapₖ_injective {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
569	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
570	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
571	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
572	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
573	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
574	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
575	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q) :
576	    Function.Injective (localStepMapₖ k hPU hstep) := by
577	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
578	  intro q
579	  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ q
580	  intro hq
581	  rw [localStepMapₖ, Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero,
582	    Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, Submodule.coe_inclusion,
583	    mem_orderGeSub] at hq
584	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
585	    mem_sectionSub]
586	  have hmem : (g : X.functionField) ∈
587	      sectionOfDivisor U D' ⊓ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) :=
588	    AddSubgroup.mem_inf.mpr ⟨g.2, hq⟩
589	  rwa [← sectionOfDivisor_inf_orderGe hPU hle hoff] at hmem
590	
591	/-- **N14 — the local step dimension is at most the residue degree.**  Given the
592	DVR residue-field identification of the single-point valuation quotient — packaged
593	as a `k`-linear embedding `ι : orderGe P (-D(P)-1) ⧸ orderGe P (-D(P)) ↪ V` into a
594	finite-dimensional `k`-vector space `V` (with `V = κ(P)` and
595	`dim_k V = deg P = [κ(P):k]` at the use site) — the local step space
596	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) ⧸ Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` has `k`-dimension at most `dim_k V`.
597	
598	The proof composes the two injections `Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D)) ↪ κ(P)-target ↪ V`:
599	`localStepMapₖ_injective` (the elementary kernel computation) and the residue
600	embedding `ι` (the DVR layer), reading off the `finrank` inequality.  The residue
601	finiteness `Module.Finite k V` is a binder here (`[κ(P):k] < ∞` for a closed point of a
602	finite-type curve) and is not proved in this file; it is discharged for a curve over an
603	algebraically closed base in `Adelic/ResidueField.lean`
604	(`finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`). -/
605	theorem localStep_finrank_le_residueEmbedding {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
606	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
607	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
608	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
609	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
610	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
611	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
612	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
613	    {V : Type u} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [Module.Finite k V]
614	    (ι : localStepTgt k P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) →ₗ[k] V)
615	    (hι : Function.Injective ι) :
616	    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k U D D') ≤ Module.finrank k V := by
617	  haveI : Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)) :=
618	    Module.Finite.of_injective ι hι
619	  refine (LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective
620	    (localStepMapₖ_injective k hPU hstep hle hoff)).trans ?_
621	  exact LinearMap.finrank_le_finrank_of_injective hι
622	
623	/-! ### N14b — the residue field `κ(P)` and the residue-degree bound
624	
625	`localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1` is the DVR residue field
626	`κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P`, realised as a `k`-subquotient of `K(X)`; its `k`-dimension is the
627	residue degree `deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.  For any `m`, multiplication by a rational
628	function `t` with `ord_P t = 1 - m` (which exists by `exists_order_eq` — the
629	intrinsic uniformizer-power order, *no* distinguished global uniformizer) carries
630	`orderGe P (m-1)` into `orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence
631	descends to the `k`-linear embedding `localStepTgt k P m ↪ κ(P)`.  Feeding it to
632	`localStep_finrank_le_residueEmbedding` completes node N14:
633	`dim_k (Γ(U,𝒪(D')) / Γ(U,𝒪(D))) ≤ deg P`. -/
634	
635	/-- **The residue degree `deg P := [κ(P) : k] = dim_k κ(P)`**, with the residue
636	field `κ(P) = 𝒪_P/𝔪_P` realised as the single-uniformizer-step valuation quotient
637	`localStepTgt k P 1 = orderGe P 0 ⧸ orderGe P 1`. -/
638	noncomputable def residueDeg (P : X.PrimeDivisor) : ℕ :=
639	  Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P 1)
640	
641	/-- **The residue embedding `ι`** completing node N14.  Multiplication by a
642	rational function `t` of order `1 - m` at `P` carries `orderGe P (m-1)` into
643	`orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` into `orderGe P 1`, hence descends to the
644	`k`-linear map `localStepTgt k P m → κ(P) = localStepTgt k P 1` between single-point
645	valuation quotients — the uniformizer-power shift of the fractional-ideal
646	filtration.  `k`-linearity is automatic: multiplication by a fixed element of
647	`K(X)` commutes with the `k`-action. -/
648	noncomputable def residueShift {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
649	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
650	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
651	    localStepTgt k P m →ₗ[k] localStepTgt k P 1 :=
652	  Submodule.mapQ _ _
653	    (LinearMap.restrict (LinearMap.mulLeft k t)
654	      (p := orderGeSub k P (m - 1)) (q := orderGeSub k P (1 - 1))
655	      (fun x hx => by
656	        rw [mem_orderGeSub] at hx
657	        rw [LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
658	        rcases eq_or_ne x 0 with hx0 | hx0
659	        · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
660	        · exact Or.inr (by
661	            rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]
662	            have := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx
663	            linarith)))
664	    (by
665	      intro x hx
666	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, mem_orderGeSub] at hx
667	      rw [Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
668	        LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub]
669	      rcases eq_or_ne (x : X.functionField) 0 with hx0 | hx0
670	      · exact Or.inl (by rw [hx0, mul_zero])
671	      · exact Or.inr (by
672	          rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hx0, hc]
673	          have := (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hx0).mp hx
674	          linarith))
675	
676	/-- **The residue embedding is injective** (node N14, `k`-linear residue form).
677	If `t · f` lands in `orderGe P 1` then `ord_P(t·f) = (1-m) + ord_P f ≥ 1`, hence
678	`ord_P f ≥ m` and `f ∈ orderGe P m`: the kernel of the shift is exactly the tighter
679	single-point subgroup, so the induced map on the local step quotient is injective. -/
680	theorem residueShift_injective {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
681	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
682	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
683	    Function.Injective (residueShift k t ht hc) := by
684	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
685	  intro q
686	  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ q
687	  intro hq
688	  rw [residueShift, Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero,
689	    Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply, LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply,
690	    LinearMap.mulLeft_apply, mem_orderGeSub] at hq
691	  rw [Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero, Submodule.mem_comap, Submodule.subtype_apply,
692	    mem_orderGeSub]
693	  rcases eq_or_ne (g : X.functionField) 0 with hg0 | hg0
694	  · rw [hg0]; exact (orderGe P m).zero_mem
695	  · refine Or.inr ?_
696	    rcases hq with h0 | h0
697	    · exact absurd ((mul_eq_zero.mp h0).resolve_left ht) hg0
698	    · rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P ht hg0, hc] at h0
699	      linarith
700	
701	/-- **The residue embedding is surjective** (node N14, `k`-linear residue form).
702	Multiplication by the intrinsic uniformizer power `t` (order `1 - m` at `P`) is a
703	bijection of `K(X)` — inverse multiplication by `t⁻¹` — carrying `orderGe P (m-1)`
704	*onto* `orderGe P 0` and `orderGe P m` onto `orderGe P 1`.  Hence the descended map
705	`residueShift` is surjective: an isomorphism
706	`orderGe P (m-1)/orderGe P m ≅ κ(P) = orderGe P 0/orderGe P 1`. -/
707	theorem residueShift_surjective {P : X.PrimeDivisor} {m : ℤ}
708	    (t : X.functionField) (ht : t ≠ 0)
709	    (hc : Scheme.RationalMap.order P t = 1 - m) :
710	    Function.Surjective (residueShift k t ht hc) := by
711	  intro z
712	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
713	  have hmem : t⁻¹ * (y : X.functionField) ∈ orderGe P (m - 1) := by
714	    rcases eq_or_ne (y : X.functionField) 0 with hy0 | hy0
715	    · rw [hy0, mul_zero]; exact (orderGe P (m - 1)).zero_mem
716	    · refine (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero (mul_ne_zero (inv_ne_zero ht) hy0)).mpr ?_
717	      have hy : (1 - 1 : ℤ) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (y : X.functionField) :=
718	        (mem_orderGe_of_ne_zero hy0).mp y.2
719	      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_mul_of_ne_zero P (inv_ne_zero ht) hy0,
720	        Scheme.RationalMap.order_inv, hc]
721	      linarith
722	  refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨t⁻¹ * (y : X.functionField),
723	    (mem_orderGeSub k).mpr hmem⟩, ?_⟩
724	  rw [residueShift, Submodule.mapQ_apply]
725	  congr 1
726	  apply Subtype.ext
727	  rw [LinearMap.coe_restrict_apply, LinearMap.mulLeft_apply]
728	  exact mul_inv_cancel_left₀ ht _
729	
730	/-- **The single-point valuation quotient has dimension `deg P` for every shift.**
731	Multiplication by an intrinsic uniformizer power intertwines the steps of the
732	fractional-ideal filtration, so every one-step valuation quotient
733	`orderGe P (m-1)/orderGe P m` is `k`-isomorphic to the residue field
734	`κ(P) = orderGe P 0/orderGe P 1`; hence they all share the residue degree
735	`deg P = [κ(P):k]`.  (`residueShift` is a bijection: injective by
736	`residueShift_injective`, surjective by `residueShift_surjective`.) -/
737	theorem finrank_localStepTgt (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (m : ℤ) :
738	    Module.finrank k (localStepTgt k P m) = residueDeg k P := by
739	  obtain ⟨t, ht, htord⟩ := exists_order_eq P (1 - m)
740	  rw [residueDeg]
741	  exact (LinearEquiv.ofBijective (residueShift k t ht htord)
742	    ⟨residueShift_injective k t ht htord, residueShift_surjective k t ht htord⟩).finrank_eq
743	
744	/-- **N14 — the local step dimension is at most the residue degree.**  For the
745	one-point twist `D' = D + P` (with `P ∈ U`, `D'(P) = D(P) + 1`, `D = D'` off `P`)
746	the local step space `Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) / Γ(U, 𝒪(D))` has `k`-dimension at most the
747	residue degree `deg P = [κ(P) : k]`.  This is the honest conclusion of N14: the
748	composite of the elementary kernel injection (`localStepMapₖ_injective`) with the
749	uniformizer-power residue embedding (`residueShift_injective`).  The finiteness of
750	`κ(P)` over `k` — `[κ(P):k] < ∞`, the residue field of a closed point of a
751	finite-type `k`-curve — enters as the binder `[Module.Finite k κ(P)]` and is not proved in
752	this file.
753	
754	It is no longer an open gate, though.  `Adelic/ResidueField.lean` proves it for a prime
755	divisor of a curve over an algebraically closed base
756	(`finite_localStepTgt_one_of_isAlgClosed_curve`), and more generally from approximation by
757	constants alone (`finite_localStepTgt_one_of_hasRationalResidues`) — the quotient is spanned
758	by the class of `1`, so finiteness is a *consequence* of the residue statement rather than a
759	prerequisite for it.  The binder is kept here rather than replaced by a global instance, so
760	that this file stays independent of the curve hypotheses and because a global instance would
761	fire during synthesis inside every lane statement; see the instance-diamond note in that
762	module. -/
763	theorem localStep_finrank_le {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
764	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
765	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
766	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
767	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
768	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
769	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
770	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
771	    [Module.Finite k (localStepTgt k P 1)] :
772	    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k U D D') ≤ residueDeg k P := by
773	  obtain ⟨t, ht, htord⟩ :=
774	    exists_order_eq P (1 - (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P))
775	  exact localStep_finrank_le_residueEmbedding k hPU hstep hle hoff
776	    (residueShift k t ht htord) (residueShift_injective k t ht htord)
777	
778	/-! ### N14 (equality direction) — the residue map is onto: strong approximation
779	
780	The `≤` bound above is the elementary half.  The reverse — that the local step space
781	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D))` fills *all* of the residue field `κ(P)` — is the surjectivity
782	of the local residue map, i.e. the **strong/weak-approximation** input: any prescribed
783	residue at `P` (any `y` with `ord_P y ≥ -n-1`) is realised, to residue precision at
784	`P` (modulo `orderGe P (-n)`), by a global-on-`U` section of `𝒪(D')`.  We take this
785	existence as the honest hypothesis `hsurj` (discharged at the use site from the
786	Dedekind-chart CRT / weak approximation for the finitely many constraint places), and
787	from it obtain the local isomorphism and the exact dimension count `= deg P`. -/
788	
789	/-- **N14 (equality direction) — the `k`-linear local step map is surjective.**  Given
790	the strong-approximation existence hypothesis `hsurj` — every rational function of
791	order `≥ -n-1` at `P` is matched, modulo `orderGe P (-n)` (to residue precision at
792	`P`), by a section of `𝒪(D')` on `U` — the residue map
793	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D)) → orderGe P (-n-1)/orderGe P (-n)` is onto. -/
794	theorem localStepMapₖ_surjective {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
795	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
796	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
797	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
798	    (hsurj : ∀ y : X.functionField,
799	        y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) →
800	        ∃ f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D',
801	          f - y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)) :
802	    Function.Surjective (localStepMapₖ k hPU hstep) := by
803	  intro z
804	  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := Submodule.Quotient.mk_surjective _ z
805	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfy⟩ := hsurj (y : X.functionField) ((mem_orderGeSub k).mp y.2)
806	  refine ⟨Submodule.Quotient.mk ⟨f, (mem_sectionSub k).mpr hf⟩, ?_⟩
807	  rw [localStepMapₖ, Submodule.mapQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.eq, Submodule.mem_comap,
808	    Submodule.subtype_apply, AddSubgroupClass.coe_sub, Submodule.coe_inclusion,
809	    mem_orderGeSub]
810	  exact hfy
811	
812	/-- **N14 (equality direction) — the local step has dimension exactly `deg P`.**  Under
813	the strong-approximation surjectivity `hsurj`, the `k`-linear local step map
814	`Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D)) → orderGe P (-n-1)/orderGe P (-n)` is bijective (injective by
815	`localStepMapₖ_injective`, surjective by `localStepMapₖ_surjective`), so the local step
816	space is `k`-isomorphic to the single-point valuation quotient, whose dimension is the
817	residue degree (`finrank_localStepTgt`):
818	`dim_k(Γ(U,𝒪(D'))/Γ(U,𝒪(D))) = deg P = [κ(P):k]`.  This is the exact one-point count
819	underlying `χ(D+P) = χ(D) + deg P`; no finiteness gate is needed (a linear equivalence,
820	whose `finrank` equality is unconditional). -/
821	theorem localStep_finrank_eq {U : X.Opens} {P : X.PrimeDivisor}
822	    (hPU : P.point ∈ U) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
823	    (hstep : (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P =
824	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P + 1)
825	    (hle : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q ≤
826	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
827	    (hoff : ∀ Q : X.PrimeDivisor, Q ≠ P →
828	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) Q = (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') Q)
829	    (hsurj : ∀ y : X.functionField,
830	        y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P - 1) →
831	        ∃ f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D',
832	          f - y ∈ orderGe P (-(show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)) :
833	    Module.finrank k (localStepDom k U D D') = residueDeg k P := by
834	  rw [(LinearEquiv.ofBijective (localStepMapₖ k hPU hstep)
835	      ⟨localStepMapₖ_injective k hPU hstep hle hoff,
836	        localStepMapₖ_surjective k hPU hstep hsurj⟩).finrank_eq,
837	    finrank_localStepTgt]
838	
839	end BaseField

841	/-! ## §N15 backbone. The 4-term exact-sequence alternating dimension identity
842	
843	The χ-additivity of the twist ledger is the alternating-dimension identity of the
844	four-term exact sequence
845	`0 → L(D')/L(D) → 𝒜(D')/𝒜(D) → Ȟ¹(D) → Ȟ¹(D') → 0`.  We isolate the pure
846	linear-algebra content: for any exact sequence of four finite-dimensional
847	`k`-vector spaces, the alternating sum of dimensions vanishes.  This is the engine
848	that telescopes `χ(D) := ℓ(D) − h¹(D)`. -/
849	
850	section ExactDim
851	
852	variable {k A B C E : Type*} [DivisionRing k]
853	    [AddCommGroup A] [Module k A] [AddCommGroup B] [Module k B]
854	    [AddCommGroup C] [Module k C] [AddCommGroup E] [Module k E]
855	    [FiniteDimensional k B] [FiniteDimensional k C]
856	
857	/-- **Alternating dimension identity of a 4-term exact sequence.** For a four-term
858	exact sequence of finite-dimensional `k`-vector spaces
859	`0 → A --i--> B --p--> C --q--> E → 0`
860	(`i` injective, exact at `B` and `C`, `q` surjective),
861	`dim A − dim B + dim C − dim E = 0`.
862	
863	The proof is a double application of rank–nullity: `dim(ker p) = dim(range i) =
864	dim A` and `dim(ker q) = dim C − dim E`, and exactness `range p = ker q` matches

1165	with `deg_k D = Σ deg Pᵢ` the adelic degree (sum of residue degrees over `k`).  Feeding
1166	the resulting identity to `riemann_inequality` yields `deg_k D + χ(0) ≤ ℓ(D)`. -/
1167	theorem chi_telescope_list (L : List X.PrimeDivisor)
1168	    (hbump : ∀ (P : X.PrimeDivisor) (E : X.WeilDivisor),
1169	      chi k U₀ U₁ (pointDivisor P + E) = chi k U₀ U₁ E + residueDeg k P) :
1170	    chi k U₀ U₁ (divisorOfList L)
1171	      = chi k U₀ U₁ 0 + ((L.map (residueDeg k)).sum : ℤ) := by
1172	  induction L with
1173	  | nil => simp [divisorOfList]
1174	  | cons P L ih =>
1175	    rw [divisorOfList, hbump, ih, List.map_cons, List.sum_cons]
1176	    push_cast
1177	    ring
1178	
1179	end ChiLedgerDim
1180	
1181	end Adelic
1182	end AlgebraicGeometry

/-!
# E-iv-alg: the degree is invariant under base-field transition (gap G-D5(b), SB-5)

For the challenge curve `C : Over (Spec k)` and a `k`-algebra map `φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field
extensions of `k`, this file proves **E-iv-alg** (`informal/deg-d5b-worksheet.md` §2):

`classDeg K₂ (CechPic.map π L) = classDeg K₁ L`

for every Čech Picard class `L` of `C_{K₁}`, along the base-field transition
`π := (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  This is the invariance equality through which the
degree of a relative Picard class becomes independent of the field of definition — the
well-definedness core of `degAt` (worksheet §1).

## The ladder (worksheet §2, steps 1–5)

1. Both sides are additive in `L`; `CurveDivisor.picClass K₁` is a surjective additive class
   map, so it suffices to treat `L = picClass K₁ (single hx' 1)` (`Finsupp.induction` plus
   `picClass_single_zpow` and `classDeg_zpow`).
2. `picClass_single` presents `L` by the tracked point equations
   `pointEquations K₁ hx' (pointUniformizerData K₁ hx')`.
3. `picClass_pullback` computes `CechPic.map π L` as the class of the pulled-back system
   `pointTransitionEquations`.  Its regularity hypothesis is discharged by
   `LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors`: on **integral** schemes with `π`
   generic-to-generic, pulled equations are automatically regular — their germs at `η` are
   the injective function-field images of nonzero rational functions, and germs of nonzero
   sections on an integral scheme are nonzero.  (This subsumes the worksheet's
   flat-local-homomorphism discharge: integrality of both curves makes flatness of `π`
   unnecessary for regularity.)
4. The presentation divisor of the pulled system is supported in the fiber `π⁻¹(x')`, with
   coefficients `ord(π^♯ t)` (`pointTransitionEquations_presentation_elem_of_eq`/`_of_ne`:
   unit germs pull back to unit germs, the second chart piece's equation is `1`).
5. E-i (`classDeg_picClass`) turns both sides into divisor degrees, and the fiber-degree
   identity (†) (`sum_ordZ_residueDeg_baseFieldTransition`, SB-4) closes the computation.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn_germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors` — pulled
  local equations on integral schemes are regular (the `hreg` discharge).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pointTransitionEquations`, `AlgebraicGeometry.pointTransitionUnit` —
  the pulled tracked point system and its trivializing unit `π^♯(uniformizer)`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition` — **E-iv-alg** (the keystone).

---
      = (pointTransitionEquations C φ hx').picClass := by
    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_single K₁ hx']
    exact (Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_pullback _ _ _).symm
  have h2 : (pointTransitionEquations C φ hx').picClass
      = Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₂ (Scheme.presentationDivisor K₂
          (pointTransitionEquations C φ hx').presentation) := by
    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass_presentationDivisor,
      Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_picClass]
  rw [h1, h2, classDeg_picClass, classDeg_picClass,
    deg_presentationDivisor_pointTransition C φ hx',
    Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K₁ hx' 1, one_mul]

/-- **E-iv-alg** (worksheet §2, the keystone): the degree of a Čech Picard class of the
base-changed curve is invariant under base-field transition — for every `k`-algebra map
`φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂` of field extensions and every class `L` on `C_{K₁}`,

`classDeg K₂ (CechPic.map π L) = classDeg K₁ L`,

where `π := (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  Proved by the §2 ladder: reduce along the
surjective additive class map `CurveDivisor.picClass K₁` to one-point divisors, present the
point class by the tracked point equations, pull the presentation back along `π`, and close
with the fiber-degree identity (†). -/
theorem classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition (φ : K₁ →ₐ[k] K₂)
    (L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left.CechPic) :
    classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left) L) = classDeg K₁ L := by
  obtain ⟨D, rfl⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq K₁ L
  suffices h : ∀ f : {p : (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left //
      p ≠ genericPoint (C ⊗ overSpec k K₁).left} →₀ ℤ,
      classDeg K₂ (Scheme.CechPic.map ((C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left)
        (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ f))
        = classDeg K₁ (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass K₁ f) from h D

58	/-! ## §N2. The point valuation of a prime divisor -/
59	
60	section PointValuation
61	
62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
63	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
64	
65	/-- **N2 — the point valuation `v_P`.** For a prime divisor `P` of a scheme `X`
66	that is regular in codimension one, the DVR stalk `O_{X,P.point}` has a maximal
67	ideal in its height-one spectrum, and the associated adic valuation of the
68	function field `K(X)` is the discrete valuation `v_P : K(X) → ℤᵐ⁰` at `P`. -/
69	noncomputable def pointValuation (P : X.PrimeDivisor) :
70	    Valuation X.functionField ℤᵐ⁰ :=
71	  (IsDiscreteValuationRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk P.point)).valuation
72	    X.functionField
73	
74	/-- **N2 identification.** The project's `Scheme.RationalMap.order P` equals
75	`-log ∘ v_P`, i.e. the additive normalisation of the point valuation `v_P`. This
76	is the bridge between the `Ring.ordFrac`-based `order` and mathlib's
77	height-one-spectrum adic valuation. -/
78	theorem order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation (P : X.PrimeDivisor)
79	    (f : X.functionField) :
80	    Scheme.RationalMap.order P f = -(WithZero.log (pointValuation P f)) := by
81	  unfold Scheme.RationalMap.order pointValuation
82	  rw [Ring.ordFrac_eq_valuation_inv, WithZero.log_inv]
83	
84	/-- **The `order` ultrametric.** For nonzero `f, g` with `f + g ≠ 0`, the order of
85	the sum is at least the minimum of the orders. This is the valuation-theoretic
86	triangle inequality `v_P(f + g) ≥ min (v_P f) (v_P g)` for the additive
87	normalisation `ord_P = -log ∘ v_P`; it is what makes `sectionOfDivisor` closed
88	under addition. -/
89	theorem order_add_ge_min (P : X.PrimeDivisor) {f g : X.functionField}
90	    (hf : f ≠ 0) (hg : g ≠ 0) (hfg : f + g ≠ 0) :
91	    min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) ≤
92	      Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := by
93	  simp only [order_eq_neg_log_pointValuation]
94	  set v := pointValuation P with hv
95	  have hvf : v f ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hf
96	  have hvg : v g ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hg
97	  have hvfg : v (f + g) ≠ 0 := by simpa [hv] using (Valuation.zero_iff v).not.mpr hfg
98	  have hadd : v (f + g) ≤ max (v f) (v g) := v.map_add f g
99	  rcases le_total (v f) (v g) with h | h
100	  · have hle : v (f + g) ≤ v g := hadd.trans (by rw [max_eq_right h])
101	    have hlog : WithZero.log (v (f + g)) ≤ WithZero.log (v g) :=
102	      (WithZero.log_le_log hvfg hvg).mpr hle
103	    calc min (-(WithZero.log (v f))) (-(WithZero.log (v g)))
104	        ≤ -(WithZero.log (v g)) := min_le_right _ _
105	      _ ≤ -(WithZero.log (v (f + g))) := by linarith
106	  · have hle : v (f + g) ≤ v f := hadd.trans (by rw [max_eq_left h])
107	    have hlog : WithZero.log (v (f + g)) ≤ WithZero.log (v f) :=
108	      (WithZero.log_le_log hvfg hvf).mpr hle
109	    calc min (-(WithZero.log (v f))) (-(WithZero.log (v g)))
110	        ≤ -(WithZero.log (v f)) := min_le_left _ _
111	      _ ≤ -(WithZero.log (v (f + g))) := by linarith
112	
113	end PointValuation

115	/-! ## §N3. Riemann–Roch section subgroups `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))` -/
116	
117	section Sections
118	
119	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
120	    [Scheme.IsRegularInCodimensionOne X]
121	
122	/-- **N3 — the Riemann–Roch section subgroup `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`.** For an open
123	`U ⊆ X` and a Weil divisor `D`, the set of rational functions `f ∈ K(X)` whose
124	order along every prime divisor `P` meeting `U` is at least `-D(P)`:
125	`Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D)) = { f : f = 0 ∨ ∀ P ∈ U, ord_P f ≥ -D(P) }`.
126	
127	The `f = 0` disjunct encodes the convention `ord_P 0 = +∞` (the project's junk
128	convention gives `ord_P 0 = 0`, so the zero function must be admitted separately).
129	Closure under addition is the `order` ultrametric `order_add_ge_min`. -/
130	def sectionOfDivisor (U : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
131	    AddSubgroup X.functionField where
132	  carrier := { f | f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
133	    -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f }
134	  zero_mem' := Or.inl rfl
135	  add_mem' := by
136	    intro f g hf hg
137	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
138	    · simpa using hg
139	    rcases eq_or_ne g 0 with rfl | hgne
140	    · simpa using hf
141	    rcases eq_or_ne (f + g) 0 with h0 | h0
142	    · exact Or.inl h0
143	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
144	    have hcf := (hf.resolve_left hfne) P hP
145	    have hcg := (hg.resolve_left hgne) P hP
146	    calc -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
147	        ≤ min (Scheme.RationalMap.order P f) (Scheme.RationalMap.order P g) :=
148	          le_min hcf hcg
149	      _ ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P (f + g) := order_add_ge_min P hfne hgne h0
150	  neg_mem' := by
151	    intro f hf
152	    rcases hf with rfl | hf
153	    · exact Or.inl (by simp)
154	    · refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
155	      rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_neg]
156	      exact hf P hP
157	
158	/-- Membership in `Γ(U, 𝒪_X(D))`. -/
159	theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
160	    {f : X.functionField} :
161	    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ f = 0 ∨ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
162	      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f :=
163	  Iff.rfl
164	
165	/-- Membership for a nonzero function: only the order condition remains. -/
166	theorem mem_sectionOfDivisor_of_ne_zero {U : X.Opens} {D : X.WeilDivisor}
167	    {f : X.functionField} (hf : f ≠ 0) :
168	    f ∈ sectionOfDivisor U D ↔ ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, P.point ∈ U →
169	      -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P) ≤ Scheme.RationalMap.order P f := by
170	  rw [mem_sectionOfDivisor, or_iff_right hf]
171	
172	/-- **Monotonicity in the divisor.** If `D ≤ D'` pointwise then
173	`Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ⊆ Γ(U, 𝒪(D'))`. -/
174	theorem sectionOfDivisor_mono (U : X.Opens) {D D' : X.WeilDivisor}
175	    (h : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P ≤
176	      (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) :
177	    sectionOfDivisor U D ≤ sectionOfDivisor U D' := by
178	  intro f hf
179	  rcases hf with rfl | hf
180	  · exact Or.inl rfl
181	  exact Or.inr fun P hP => (neg_le_neg (h P)).trans (hf P hP)
182	
183	/-- **`1 ∈ Γ(U, 𝒪(0))`** — the seed of `L(0) ⊇ k`. -/
184	theorem one_mem_sectionOfDivisor_zero (U : X.Opens) :
185	    (1 : X.functionField) ∈ sectionOfDivisor U (0 : X.WeilDivisor) := by
186	  refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
187	  rw [Scheme.RationalMap.order_one]
188	  change -((0 : X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ) P) ≤ 0
189	  simp
190	
191	/-- **Intersection over opens.** A section over `U₁ ⊔ U₂` is exactly a section
192	over `U₁` intersected with a section over `U₂`. -/
193	theorem sectionOfDivisor_sup (U₁ U₂ : X.Opens) (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
194	    sectionOfDivisor (U₁ ⊔ U₂) D =
195	      sectionOfDivisor U₁ D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U₂ D := by
196	  ext f
197	  rw [AddSubgroup.mem_inf, mem_sectionOfDivisor, mem_sectionOfDivisor,
198	    mem_sectionOfDivisor]
199	  constructor
200	  · rintro (rfl | h)
201	    · exact ⟨Or.inl rfl, Or.inl rfl⟩
202	    · exact ⟨Or.inr fun P hP => h P (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup.mpr (Or.inl hP)),
203	        Or.inr fun P hP => h P (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup.mpr (Or.inr hP))⟩
204	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
205	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
206	    · exact Or.inl rfl
207	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
208	    rcases (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup).mp hP with hP1 | hP2
209	    · exact (h1.resolve_left hfne) P hP1
210	    · exact (h2.resolve_left hfne) P hP2
211	
212	/-- **Intersection of divisor conditions is the `min` divisor.** If `E` is the
213	pointwise minimum of `D` and `D'`, then `Γ(U, 𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U, 𝒪(D')) = Γ(U, 𝒪(E))`,
214	i.e. `L(D) ∩ L(D') = L(min D D')`. -/
215	theorem sectionOfDivisor_inf_divisor (U : X.Opens) {D D' E : X.WeilDivisor}
216	    (hE : ∀ P : X.PrimeDivisor, (show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P =
217	      min ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
218	        ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P)) :
219	    sectionOfDivisor U D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U D' = sectionOfDivisor U E := by
220	  ext f
221	  rw [AddSubgroup.mem_inf, mem_sectionOfDivisor, mem_sectionOfDivisor,
222	    mem_sectionOfDivisor]
223	  constructor
224	  · rintro ⟨h1, h2⟩
225	    rcases eq_or_ne f 0 with rfl | hfne
226	    · exact Or.inl rfl
227	    refine Or.inr fun P hP => ?_
228	    rw [hE P]
229	    rcases le_total ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D) P)
230	        ((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from D') P) with hle | hle
231	    · rw [min_eq_left hle]; exact (h1.resolve_left hfne) P hP
232	    · rw [min_eq_right hle]; exact (h2.resolve_left hfne) P hP
233	  · rintro (rfl | h)
234	    · exact ⟨Or.inl rfl, Or.inl rfl⟩
235	    · exact ⟨Or.inr fun P hP =>
236	          ((by rw [hE P]; exact neg_le_neg (min_le_left _ _)) :
237	            _ ≤ -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P)).trans (h P hP),
238	        Or.inr fun P hP =>
239	          ((by rw [hE P]; exact neg_le_neg (min_le_right _ _)) :
240	            _ ≤ -((show X.PrimeDivisor →₀ ℤ from E) P)).trans (h P hP)⟩
241	
242	/-- **The Riemann–Roch space `L(D)`.** Global sections of `𝒪_X(D)`: the section
243	over all of `X`. On a 2-affine cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤` this is
244	`Γ(U₀, 𝒪(D)) ⊓ Γ(U₁, 𝒪(D))`, the kernel of the Čech difference map. -/
245	def linearSystem (D : X.WeilDivisor) : AddSubgroup X.functionField :=
246	  sectionOfDivisor ⊤ D
247	
248	/-- On a 2-affine cover `U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤`, `L(D)` is the intersection of the two
249	chart sections. -/
250	theorem linearSystem_eq_inf {U₀ U₁ : X.Opens} (hcov : U₀ ⊔ U₁ = ⊤)
251	    (D : X.WeilDivisor) :
252	    linearSystem D = sectionOfDivisor U₀ D ⊓ sectionOfDivisor U₁ D := by
253	  rw [linearSystem, ← hcov, sectionOfDivisor_sup]
254	
255	end Sections

257	/-! ## §N1. Dedekind coordinate rings of affine charts -/
258	
259	section Chart
260	
261	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
262	
263	/-- **N1 (unconditional half) — the affine chart is a fraction-ring chart.** For a
264	nonempty affine open `U` of an integral scheme, the coordinate ring `Γ(X, U)` has
265	`K(X)` as its fraction field. Thin wrapper around mathlib's
266	`functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen`. -/
267	theorem chartRing_isFractionRing [IsIntegral X] {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
268	    [Nonempty U] : IsFractionRing Γ(X, U) X.functionField :=
269	  functionField_isFractionRing_of_isAffineOpen X U hU
270	
271	/-- **N1 (unconditional half) — the affine chart is Noetherian.** For a nonempty
272	affine open `U` of a locally Noetherian scheme, `Γ(X, U)` is a Noetherian ring. -/
273	theorem chartRing_isNoetherianRing [IsLocallyNoetherian X] {U : X.Opens}
274	    (hU : IsAffineOpen U) : IsNoetherianRing Γ(X, U) :=
275	  IsLocallyNoetherian.component_noetherian ⟨U, hU⟩
276	
277	/-- **N1 — the Dedekind-from-DVR bridge** (pure ring theory, `IsDedekindDomainDvr`).
278	A Noetherian integral domain whose localization at every nonzero prime is a
279	discrete valuation ring is a Dedekind domain. This is exactly the criterion under
280	which a smooth (equivalently: regular, on a curve) affine chart `Γ(X, U)` is
281	Dedekind; the missing input is that every nonzero prime of the chart is
282	height-one, i.e. that `X` is a curve. -/
283	theorem isDedekindDomain_of_forall_localization_dvr {R : Type*} [CommRing R]
284	    [IsDomain R] [IsNoetherianRing R]
285	    (h : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime], P ≠ ⊥ →
286	      IsDiscreteValuationRing (Localization.AtPrime P)) :
287	    IsDedekindDomain R := by
288	  haveI : IsDedekindDomainDvr R := by
289	    refine { is_dvr_at_nonzero_prime := fun P hP hPp => ?_ }

312	/-! ## §N4. Finiteness of the places of a rational function on a chart
313	
314	The scheme-level statement `rationalMap_order_finite_support` in
315	`RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor.lean` (that `P ↦ ord_P f` has finite support) is **false**
316	as pinned there with only `[IsLocallyNoetherian X]`: the "line with infinitely many
317	origins" is integral, locally Noetherian and regular in codimension one, yet `t`
318	has order one at each of its infinitely many origins.  Finiteness needs `X`
319	globally Noetherian (`[IsNoetherian X]`, i.e. quasi-compact), matching Stacks 02RV.
320	
321	What *is* unconditionally true, and is the reusable core of the affine-chart
322	argument, is the following: on a single Dedekind chart, a nonzero rational function
323	is non-integral (valuation `≠ 1`) at only finitely many height-one places. -/

325	section Finiteness
326	
327	variable {R : Type*} [CommRing R] [IsDedekindDomain R]
328	    {K : Type*} [Field K] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
329	
330	/-- **N4 (chart core).** For a nonzero element `k` of the fraction field of a
331	Dedekind domain `R`, only finitely many height-one places `v` have `v(k) ≠ 1`
332	(i.e. only finitely many places where `k` is a zero or a pole). This is the
333	finite-support statement for the principal divisor on a single affine chart,
334	obtained from mathlib's `HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite` applied to `k` and to
335	`k⁻¹`. -/
336	theorem finite_places_ne_one {k : K} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
337	    {v : HeightOneSpectrum R | v.valuation K k ≠ 1}.Finite := by
338	  have h1 := HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite R k
339	  have h2 := HeightOneSpectrum.Support.finite R k⁻¹
340	  refine (h1.union h2).subset fun v hv => ?_
341	  simp only [HeightOneSpectrum.Support, Set.mem_setOf_eq] at hv ⊢
342	  rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hv with hlt | hgt
343	  · right
344	    rw [Set.mem_setOf_eq, map_inv₀]
345	    have hv0 : v.valuation K k ≠ 0 := by
346	      simpa using (Valuation.zero_iff (v.valuation K)).not.mpr hk
347	    exact one_lt_inv₀ (lt_of_le_of_ne zero_le (Ne.symm hv0)) |>.mpr hlt
348	  · exact Or.inl hgt
349	
350	end Finiteness

/-!
# The base-field window transport pack — DDR-2's `N`-pack (DAT-D `dd4`/`ddr`)

The abstract fibre window divisor `N` of DDR-2's certified-degree pinch
(`RiemannRoch/CarveDegree.lean`), built for any field extension `K/k`: an honest Weil
divisor on `relCurve C K` carrying the **transported** DD-0 window facts of the `k`-level
embedding window `M·F`.  Per I-0204's binding architectural finding, the per-field ledger
constants do *not* transport (`windowM_choice` is a per-field `Classical.choose`), so `N`
is produced by transporting window **facts**, not by re-running the `K`-level ledger:

* the `k`-level `H¹` inputs enter through the landed twist-pair collapse
  (`relThetaPairH1_windowM`, `subsingleton_relThetaPairH1`) and cross into the datum
  world by the whole-chart theta datum (`Cohomology/RelCurveCollapse.lean`);
* the datum base-changes to `K` (`datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange`), where the
  presentation bridge (`presentationSheafIso` + `subsingleton_hModule_gluedSheaf_one_iff`)
  extracts an honest divisor `windowTransportDivisor C K π a` with vanishing `H¹`;
* its class is the transported theta class (`cechPicClass_baseChange` + the collapse
  class law), so its degree is `a·δ` by E-iv-alg
  (`classDeg_cechPicMap_baseFieldTransition`) and W7-B3 (`classDeg_cechPicMap_of_isIso`);
* the `K`-level normalization windows come from the π-free peeling
  (`subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness`, the abstract-witness form of DAT-0a's
  `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`) at the transported
  multiplier window `s·F`, licensed by ledger arithmetic.

import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.Divisor

/-!
# The principal divisor of a rational function on a curve

For a scheme `X` smooth of relative dimension one over a field `K` and integral (the curve
bundle of the Jacobian challenge), a nonzero rational function `g : K(X)ˣ` has a well-defined
**principal divisor** `div(g) = ∑ₓ ordₓ(g) · x`, a finitely supported `ℤ`-valued function on
the closed points:

* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.ordZ`: the `ℤ`-valued order of a unit of the function field at a
  closed point, packaged as a group homomorphism `K(X)ˣ →* Multiplicative ℤ`;
* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.divOf`: the principal divisor `div(g)`, whose value at a closed
  point `x` is the classical order `ordₓ(g)`, with additivity `divOf_mul` and `divOf_one`.

## Sign convention

Mathlib's `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation` sends a local uniformizer `π` to
`WithZero.exp (-1) = ↑(Multiplicative.ofAdd (-1))`, i.e. the *additive* value of the valuation
of a uniformizer is `-1`.  The **classical order** used here is the negative of that additive
value: `ordZ` is defined as the inverse (in the multiplicative group `Multiplicative ℤ`) of the
units-extraction of `Scheme.ord`, so that

  `Multiplicative.toAdd (ordZ f hx π) = +1`   for `π` (the image of) a uniformizer,

a *zero* of `g` contributing a positive order and a *pole* a negative one.  Consequently
`divOf f g ⟨x, hx⟩ = Multiplicative.toAdd (ordZ f hx g)` is the classical order of vanishing.

## Finiteness

The support of `div(g)` is finite: represent `g` by a section `s` on a nonempty open `U` (the
generic point lies in every nonempty open); at every closed point of the basic open set
`X.basicOpen s` the germ of `s` is a unit, so `ordₓ(g) = 0` there.  The complement is a closed
set avoiding the generic point, hence finite on the Noetherian curve.  Finiteness of the
ambient space uses `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]` together with `[QuasiCompact f]`: a principal
divisor is only finitely supported on a quasi-compact (hence Noetherian) curve, and the proper
curve of the Jacobian challenge satisfies this.  (The bare `[LocallyOfFiniteType f]` gives only
`IsLocallyNoetherian X`, which does not force the *global* space to be Noetherian without
quasi-compactness.)
-/

11	/-!
12	# `H¹` base-field invariance and base-field invariance of the genus (W5-X3)
13	
14	For the challenge curve `C` over a field `k` and a field extension `K/k`
15	(`[Field K] [Algebra k K]`), this file proves *cohomology commutes with base change* for
16	the structure sheaf **from the absolute curve**: on the Rebuild carriers
17	(`Sheaf.HModule (·.moduleKSheaf ·) n`, two-cover Čech-definitional),
18	
19	* `H⁰(C, 𝒪) ⊗[k] K ≃ₗ[K] H⁰(C_K, 𝒪)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.h0BaseFieldEquiv`),
20	* `H¹(C, 𝒪) ⊗[k] K ≃ₗ[K] H¹(C_K, 𝒪)` (`AlgebraicGeometry.h1BaseFieldEquiv`),
21	
22	and deduces that **the genus is invariant under base field extension**
23	(`AlgebraicGeometry.genus_baseField`): the genus of `C_K = (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left`,
24	viewed as a legal curve over `K` through the `Curve.BaseChangeInstances` stack
25	(`baseChangeBundle C K`), equals `genus C`. The dimension count is scalar-identity-first
26	(W12 discipline): the one `finrank` identity is
27	`AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField`, with the `= genus C` form
28	`AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` for the Wave-5 tangent count
29	(`dim T₀(J_k̄) = genus C`).
30	
31	The engine is the flat/free cohomology-and-base-change mechanism of the landed
32	`Cohomology.RelativeH1BaseChange` (w4-2), run once more with the *absolute* curve as
33	source — NOT Mumford II.5 (no semicontinuity, no Exchange): the two-term Čech complex of
34	an affine two-cover base-changes termwise by the landed free identification
35	`relSectionsBaseChange` (`Γ(C, V) ⊗[k] R ≃ₗ[R] Γ(C_R, V_R)`), and `H¹` is its cokernel,
36	which commutes with any base change by right-exactness
37	(`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`). The intermediate statements are proved for an
38	arbitrary commutative `k`-algebra `R` (the `k → R` legs of the CBC ladder; the tower legs
39	`R → R'` are the landed `relH1BaseChange`), so the dual-numbers lane (`R = k[ε]`) can
40	consume them as well.
41	
42	## Main declarations
43	
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relPullbackSection_resHom` — pullback of sections to the relative
45	  curve commutes with restriction.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveDiffBaseChange` — **CBC-1 (`k → R`, the commuting square)**:
47	  the base change of the absolute two-cover restriction-difference map is carried to the
48	  relative difference map under the term equivalences.
49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH1CokBaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`), cokernel form**:
50	  `R ⊗[k] H1Cok k C ≃ₗ[R] H1Cok R C_R`, with the computation rule
51	  `curveH1CokBaseChange_tmul_mk`.
52	* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH1BaseChange` — **CBC-2 (`i = 1`) on the cohomology carriers**:
53	  `R ⊗[k] H¹(C, 𝒪) ≃ₗ[R] H¹(C_R, 𝒪)` for every commutative `k`-algebra `R`.
54	* `AlgebraicGeometry.curveH0BaseChange` — the degree-zero analogue, free of charge from
55	  `relSectionsBaseChange` at `V = ⊤` (`C` proper makes `⊤` qcqs).
56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.h1BaseFieldEquiv`, `AlgebraicGeometry.h0BaseFieldEquiv` — the
57	  headline field-extension statements, keyed on the `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` spelling of
58	  `Curve.BaseChangeInstances`.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField`, `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h0_baseField`,
60	  `AlgebraicGeometry.finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` — the scalar `finrank` identities.
61	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus_baseField` — `genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C`.
62	
63	## Implementation notes
64	
65	The `k`-module structure on the absolute sections `Γ(C.left, V)` appears in two
66	definitionally equal presentations: `Scheme.overModule` under the
67	`letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom` of the frozen `genus` spelling (the
68	two-cover/`moduleKSheaf` side) and `Over.sectionsAlgebra` (the `relSectionsBaseChange`
69	side). Statements are given in the `genus`/two-cover spelling; the seams are crossed by
70	`exact`, as in `Cohomology.RelativeH1BaseChange` (see the transparency note there).
71	-/
72	
73	set_option autoImplicit false
74	/- Statements mix `Γ(relCurve C R, ·)` with opens produced on the product spelling
75	`(C ⊗ overSpec k R).left`, and the two presentations of the `k`-module structure on
76	`Γ(C.left, V)`; see the module docstring and `Cohomology.RelativeSectionsLinear`. -/

93	/-- **Pullback of sections to the relative curve commutes with restriction**: for
94	`W ≤ V ⊆ C.left`, restricting on the curve and then pulling back along the first
95	projection agrees with pulling back and then restricting on the relative curve. -/
96	lemma relPullbackSection_resHom {W V : C.left.Opens} (hWV : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(C.left, V)) :
97	    relPullbackSection C R W (C.left.resHom hWV s) =
98	      (relCurve C R).resHom
99	        (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k R)).left hWV)
100	        (relPullbackSection C R V s) := by
101	  have h1 : C.left.presheaf.map (homOfLE hWV).op ≫
102	      (fst C (overSpec k R)).left.appLE W ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W) le_rfl =
103	      (fst C (overSpec k R)).left.appLE V ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W)
104	        (le_rfl.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k R)).left hWV)) :=
105	    Scheme.Hom.map_appLE _ le_rfl (homOfLE hWV).op
106	  have h2 : (fst C (overSpec k R)).left.appLE V ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ V)
107	        le_rfl ≫
108	      (relCurve C R).presheaf.map
109	        (homOfLE (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k R)).left hWV)).op =
110	      (fst C (overSpec k R)).left.appLE V ((fst C (overSpec k R)).left ⁻¹ᵁ W)
111	        (le_rfl.trans (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k R)).left hWV)) :=
112	    Scheme.Hom.appLE_map _ le_rfl
113	      (homOfLE (Scheme.Hom.preimage_mono (fst C (overSpec k R)).left hWV)).op
114	  exact (congr($(h1).hom s)).trans (congr($(h2).hom s)).symm
115	
116	variable (D : C.left.AffineTwoCover)
117	
118	/-- The base change of the absolute two-cover complex's degree-zero term: the product of
119	the two chart-term identifications `relSectionsBaseChange`,
120	`R ⊗[k] (Γ(C, V₀) × Γ(C, V₁)) ≃ₗ[R] Γ(C_R, V₀ᴿ) × Γ(C_R, V₁ᴿ)`. -/

1	/-
